title: Establishment of age- and sex-stratified normative data for the Brief Assessment of Cognition (BAC) app in healthy Japanese individuals

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Establishment of age- and sex-stratified normative data for the Brief Assessment of Cognition (BAC) app in healthy Japanese individuals》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · p0055】The objective of the present study was to obtain the mean and standard deviation (SD) for each BAC App subtest within age- and sex-defined groups in healthy Japanese adolescents and adults. This will enable calculation of composite scores for Japanese individuals using the BAC App, analogous to those available for the BACS.

【Introduction · p0035】Cognitive impairment is one of the core symptoms of schizophrenia and has a substantial impact on social function (Green et al., 2012; Vita et al., 2022). A broad range of cognitive domains is affected in schizophrenia, including attention, executive function, verbal learning, memory (including working memory), and verbal fluency, and these domains are closely associated with work-related social functioning (Green, 2016). Cognitive impairment in schizophrenia is present across the course of the illness, with evidence of deficits in premorbid phases and substantial impairment after the onset of psychosis (Keefe, 2014). Approximately 70%–75% of patients with schizophrenia have neurocognitive impairments (Silberstein and Harvey, 2019). These findings underscore the continued importance of developing more effective treatments targeting cognitive impairment in schizophrenia, as well as simple and rapid cognitive assessment methods for clinical and research use.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Establishment of age- and sex-stratified normative data for the Brief Assessment of Cognition (BAC) app in healthy Japanese individuals》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Study design · p0060】This was a cross-sectional study involving healthy Japanese adolescents and adults whose estimated IQ was determined to be ≥70 based on the Japanese Adult Reading Test-25 (JART-25) assessment (Matsuoka et al., 2006; Matsuoka and Kim, 2007). The study was conducted from March 6, 2024, to March 31, 2026. Healthy volunteers were recruited between April 2024 and September 2025. The recruitment of participants was outsourced to and conducted by Buzzreach, Inc.

【Study design · p0065】The study protocol was approved by the National Center of Neurology and Psychiatry Ethics Committee (IRB11000187) and was registered with the Japan Registry of Clinical Trials under the identifier jRCT1030240378 (https://jrct.mhlw.go.jp/latest-detail/jRCT1030240378). The study adhered to the Ethical Guidelines for Medical and Biological Research Involving Human Subjects. For adults, written informed consent was obtained from participants before enrollment. For participants aged ≥16 to <18 years who had graduated from junior high school, written informed consent was obtained from both the participant and their legally authorized representative before enrollment. For participants aged <16 years who had not graduated from junior high school, written informed assent was obtained from participants, along with written consent from their legally authorized representative before enrollment.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Establishment of age- and sex-stratified normative data for the Brief Assessment of Cognition (BAC) app in healthy Japanese individuals》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · p0135】A total of 121 individuals provided written informed consent and underwent screening for eligibility, and 121 participants met the eligibility criteria. After excluding participants with missing data, 120 participants were included in the analysis population. Among the overall 120 participants, the mean age was 38.6 years, the mean JART-25 total score was 104.7, and the mean duration of education was 13.6 years (Table 1). Within each age subgroup, no notable sex differences in age, JART-25 score, or years of education were observed.

【Conclusions · p0205】The present study characterized performance on the Japanese version of the BAC App across cognitive domains in a sample of healthy native Japanese speakers. Our results also highlight characteristics of task performance across forms and verbal measures that may reflect linguistic and task-structure influences in the Japanese version of the BAC App. The present study provides foundational, standardized reference data for the Japanese version of the BAC App and supports its use as a digital cognitive assessment tool in native Japanese speakers.

Words are labeled according to their position within each list, and values indicate the proportion of correct answers.(B) Correlation coefficients of correct responses between pairs of words.Heatmaps display phi coefficients calculated for each word pair within Form 1 and Form 3, with higher values indicating stronger associations in recall patterns between words.(C) Hierarchical agglomerative cluster analysis of words.Dendrograms were generated using Ward's method based on binary recall data (correct = 1, incorrect = 0). sections.title: 复现线索
sections.text:
《Establishment of age- and sex-stratified normative data for the Brief Assessment of Cognition (BAC) app in healthy Japanese individuals》：复现时可直接核对的数据、软件或实现线索。

【Data availability · p0030】The data underlying this study are not publicly available. Requests for access to the data may be considered upon reasonable request to the corresponding author, subject to review and approval by the lead author and the sponsoring company.

【Statistical analysis · p0130】BAC App subtest scores were calculated as follows: (raw score − age- and sex-specific mean) / age- and sex-specific SD (Keefe et al., 2008). The SDs of the sum and mean of the BAC App subtest z-scores were also calculated. For the Verbal Memory Task and the Tower of London Task, tabulations were performed separately for each of the two forms used for responses, and differences with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated between forms. Based on the observed difference between forms for the Verbal Memory Task, the following additional analyses were conducted: comparison of correct response rates between forms for words presented in the same serial position; calculation of phi coefficients between pairs of words within each form, with responses coded as correct = 1 and incorrect = 0; and hierarchical agglomerative cluster analysis using Ward's method for participants aged ≥18 years, conducted separately for each form. R version 4.1 or later was used for statistical analyses. Two-sided 95% CIs were reported. No adjustments for multiplicity were made.
